outcome: Two concrete P1 defects in the new coordinator require the narrow correction below before release. Existing actual targeted2/2 and most reused execution protections are real; needs_more_work or untested matrices alone are not defects.

p1.title: Known invalid first kickoff leaves a nonrecoverable pending request through the normal UI
p1.sourceCause: A new prepared intent is written at line24 before modelReady, current copy/executor readiness and downstream complete create validators. Those known failures then throw at line25 or later. Any new command for this project is rejected KICKOFF_PENDING. Context returns no pending request/command/stage. The UI uses a transient useRef, resets it on goal/criteria/choice edits and loses it after reload, so the user cannot recover the original exact request by fixing the visible input.
p1.reachableCounterexample: Authenticated owner submits syntactically valid kickoff with unavailable model, or registered but currently unready executor, or a workspace not in current choices. No task is necessary for this failure: prepared persists. Fix configuration/selection or reload, submit a new command -> KICKOFF_PENDING; no disclosed old request to reconcile. This is static source reachability, not a newly executed test.
p1.narrowFix: Perform all known pure prerequisites and shared task/supervisor schema checks before the initial durable write. Keep genuine post-effect partial intents, but expose their exact owner-bound original command/binding/stage in read-only context and a resume/reconciliation path; UI must persist/reuse that original request rather than silently replacing its UUID. Do not delete history, clear unknown accounting or auto-start on GET.
p1.targetedRegression: Invalid model/choice/duplicate criterion creates0task/session/run and no permanent pending reservation. Existing genuine after-task cut survives reload via original exact request, not a new nonce; editing an uncommitted invalid draft can submit normally.

p1.title: Task-stage recovery adopts the current paused session revision as a fresh start authority
p1.sourceCause: When intent has stage task and sessionId null, the CONTROL_CHANGED guard is skipped. The recovery branch accepts any existing session with the same task and uses its current revision as startRevision, without requiring the original create-command receipt, untouched draft or original expected revision. The following original start command has not yet executed and action start permits a paused session.
p1.reachableCounterexample: Crash after supervisor.create has committed but before coordinator persists sessionId/stage. Intent remains task. On restart the owner pauses the visible draft, revoking authority. Retry the original kickoff: sessionId-null bypasses line25; line28 copies the paused latest revision; line29 issues first start with authorizeContinuous true and matching new revision -> re-enables the paused goal. The unchanged supervisor command accepts this sequence. This is a precise source counterexample, not a fabricated runtime observation.
p1.narrowFix: Recover the fixed supervisor.create command receipt/id/revision instead of refreshing authority from current snapshot. Replaying that original create command already returns its frozen receipt. Persist the original expected revision, then reject/control-reconcile any current session or policy changed by pause/stop/takeover/revise. Never substitute a newly observed control revision as permission for an old kickoff.
p1.targetedRegression: Inject a cut after supervisor session commit but before kickoff session-stage write; owner pause; retry original kickoff -> CONTROL_CHANGED/CAS rejection, paused policy remains revoked,0newrun. Also verify untouched draft recovers to one task/session/start with stable IDs.

implementedAndReusable.item: Read-only owner project context and explicit kickoff route are real and registered in createApp. GET does not create task/session/run, call model or pump. Principal is current administrator profile me; project owner is enforced; routes return no-store.

Task identity is durably reserved before repository create. The repository create override uses the deterministic reserved ID; pendingOwns is connected to supervisor owns before execution timers begin. Generic start, scheduler and queued preflight already consult ownership, so the demonstrated after-task cut cannot be stolen.

Fixed task/session/start child command IDs, exact fingerprint replay and complete-response replay are implemented. Completed kickoff replay after a later pause returns its old response without side effects; the saved real test covers that successful-completion case. It does not cover the session-commit cut in P1 above.

No fake cross-SQLite transaction is claimed. WAL/FULL kickoff stages and V1 task/supervisor command receipts are used. Genuine unresolved partial state is retained rather than deleting records or inventing a new task to recover.

Existing supervisor start/policy windows, signed normal terminal/evidence, model consume-once, stop confirmation, unknown/incomplete usage and experience correction paths are reused. This slice does not reset historical task usage or resume the old10-minute automation.

specificQuestions.historyTasks: There is no historyTasks all-history blocker in this fixed runtime or workbench source. Context lists existing tasks, but kickoff does not inspect/reuse them and always creates a new task when there is no supervisor. Thus all real projects are not automatically blocked. It also has not simplified continuation of an existing native task/session: owner must use the existing explicit advanced adopt/reconcile path; it must not claim the new task reuses old native history. Existing supervisor sessions are reused by normal explicit commands. Safe never-run draft reuse from the plan is not implemented in kickoff. Treat this as a clearly bounded missing convenience/continuation slice, not a proof every existing project is unusable.
specificQuestions.budgetOneDollar: Not an active1USD cap in the supported supervisor execution path. New task budget1 satisfies the legacy required TaskDTO. supervisorDispatch205 requires record-only;207 constructs budgetUSD0; preflight168 accepts project-supervisor/record-only independently of task.cost<budget; agent-runner141/144 skips USD exhaustion under recordOnly and79 removes native max-budget args. Actual costs/unknown status are unchanged. Do not present task budget1 as paid spend or an added cap.
specificQuestions.codexVsClaudeLabel: Not a proven Codex dispatch rejection: actual executorId comes from task.agent and execution205 explicitly allows claude or codex engines. supervisor.executor is still forced claude-code metadata, so its UI/experience selection label can misdescribe Codex. Actual engine should be displayed/matched honestly, but current101Claude flow is not blocked by that constant. Do not report unsupported Codex solely from create.executor literal.
specificQuestions.unknownAcknowledgment: Fresh goal policy permits acknowledgeUnknownHistory false; it does not throw solely for false. Future unknown-history continuation is still guarded by grant/window acknowledgment. No unknown counts are zeroed by this coordinator. UI acknowledgment messaging and later eligibility must stay honest.
specificQuestions.preparedRecoveryProof: Current test injects afterTask only after i.stage=task was written. It is not a prepared/reserved-ID or session/start-unknown full crash matrix. Before-task pending ownership is nevertheless explicit in source, so missing tests alone are not reported as a vulnerability.
specificQuestions.existingPausedSession: Normal GET and completed replay do not resume it. UI resume is an explicit POST and disabled for running/judging/dispatching. The narrow unrecorded-session recovery path in P1 is the specific exception requiring repair.
specificQuestions.newProjectCopyPrerequisite: API project registration defaults copies[]; context choices are only registered nonproduction copies paired with templates. A independently reviews the new UI reachability of copy registration; this API review confirms there is no implicit default-copy provisioning API. Do not claim a copy record creates or verifies a physical remote directory.
